Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corporation's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; David Rodriguez, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, VP of Exploration; Robert Hayes, VP of Marketing; and Emily Carter, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, John Smith, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corporation delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production levels and robust EBITDA growth, fueled by our Permian Basin momentum and efficient capital deployment. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on midstream infrastructure expansions and exploration successes that are adding high-quality reserves. We are focused on disciplined production growth and optimizing our capital allocation to prioritize shareholder returns through dividends and buybacks. Further, we are working on cost efficiencies and debt reduction to strengthen our balance sheet. We continue to adjust to market dynamics like easing takeaway constraints and LNG demand. We are advancing our drilling program with exceptional well results in key basins. Finally, we are taking steps to enhance sustainability, including emissions reductions and CCUS initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year. Operating income was $2.1 billion, and net income was $1.4 billion. We generated $1.6 billion in free cash flow and returned $900 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $12.4 billion in total debt and $2.5 billion in cash.

Good morning, everyone. Let me walk you through our adjusted EBITDA first, which came in at $2.45 billion for the quarter, reflecting a robust 28% year-over-year increase from $1.91 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our strongest quarterly performance since the post-pandemic recovery peak, driven by higher production volumes, favorable realized pricing, and disciplined cost management across our upstream portfolio. Production volumes contributed about 45% of the YoY uplift, or roughly $240 million, with averages of 525,000 BOE/d, up 18% from 445,000 BOE/d last year. This was led by Permian Basin assets where D&C activity ramped to 28 rigs from 22 a year ago, delivering first oil from 145 new horizontal wells in the Delaware and Midland sub-basins, with Wolfcamp and Bone Spring laterals averaging 12,000 feet and IP rates exceeding 1,800 BOE/d per well thanks to optimized frac designs with more ceramic proppant and tighter stage spacing. Internationally, offshore Brazil added incremental 25,000 BOE/d from Buzios Phase 3 via subsea tie-backs to our FPSO. Eagle Ford dipped slightly due to Hurricane Idalia impacts but we've restored 95%.

Realized pricing added another 35%, or about $200 million, with blended oil at $78.50 per barrel, up 17% from $67.20, tracking dated Brent at $82/bbl amid OPEC+ cuts of 3.66 million bpd and Red Sea premiums. Gas realizations improved to $3.45 per Mcf from $2.90 on Henry Hub spots and 60% hedging at $3.20 floor, plus $1.20/bbl from marketing basis trades as Waha discounts narrowed. Cost efficiencies delivered $150 million tailwinds, with LOE per BOE down 12% to $8.50 via Permian electrification covering 40% of pads, slashing diesel by 25% and emissions by 15%. G&A dropped 8% to $1.10/BOE through AI predictive maintenance reducing downtime 20%, DD&A steady at $18.50/BOE. One-time gains included $50 million from Bakken divestiture and $30 million from North Sea liability settlements. Permian drove 60% of growth with $52/BOE cash margins, Brazil added high-margin barrels at $15/BOE LOE, North Sea flat amid UK tax hikes but advancing EOR CO2 pilots.

On production volumes, we're reporting average daily output of 525,000 BOE per day for the quarter, a solid 2% increase quarter-over-quarter from 515,000 BOE/d in Q2, and 11% year-over-year from 473,000 BOE/d in Q3 2023. Oil production averaged 320,000 bbl/d, up 3% QoQ from 310,000 and 19% YoY from 269,000. Natural gas held at 1.2 Bcf/d or 200,000 BOE/d, flat QoQ and YoY amid weak $2.35/MMBtu Henry Hub pricing. Permian, 72% of volumes, surged with Delaware oil up 5% QoQ to 230,000 bbl/d from six new pads using 'Apex-XL' completions: 15,000-foot laterals, 80 lbs/ft proppant, boosting IP30s 25% with EURs of 1.2-1.5 MMBOE. YoY Permian up 15% post-$450 million bolt-on of 20,000 net acres. Eagle Ford oil grew 2% QoQ to 60,000 bbl/d from refracs with 40% IP uplift. Bakken and GoM had minor declines from ESP issues and Hurricane Francine.

Turning to debt levels, total debt stood at $12.4 billion as of September 30, comprising $9.8 billion in senior notes, $2.1 billion revolver, and $0.5 billion JV obligations—a 7% QoQ drop from $13.3 billion via maturities and paydowns from $1.2 billion FCF. YoY down 15% from $14.6 billion. Maturity profile: 12% in next 12 months, 4.8-year average, 4.9% cost down 40 bps. Net debt at $9.7 billion, down $1.1 billion QoQ, 1.2x to TTM EBITDAX of $8.1 billion from 1.5x YE2023. Debt-to-cap 28%, fixed charge coverage 5.5x. Recent $1.75 billion sustainability bond at 5.25% refinanced higher notes.

For capital allocation priorities, our framework is first fortress balance sheet, then dividends and buybacks, then reinvestment. Q3 FCF of $1.6 billion deployed $3.8 billion YTD. Dividends grew 15% YoY to $0.45/share quarterly, $1.80 annualized, 3.5% yield at 35% FCF payout. Buybacks executed $1.1 billion YTD of $4 billion program at avg $52/share, retiring 2.1% shares. Reinvestment $1.8 billion: $1.3 billion upstream (Permian $850 million for 120 wells, Guyana $300 million, North Sea $150 million), $350 million midstream/tech like Pecos JV and CCUS, $150 million bolt-ons.

On production guidance, for Q4 2024 we expect 530,000 to 540,000 BOE/d, 2-4% up from Q3's 525,000, with oil 325-335 Mbbl/d (64%), NGLs 60-65 Mbbl/d, gas 2.5-2.6 Bcf/d. Full year 1.16-1.24 MMBOE/d, 3-7% over 2023. Driven by Permian TILs of 45-50 wells at 1,200-1,400 boe/d IP, Eagle Ford pilots adding 8-10 Mbbl/d, GoM steady. Factors: Permian efficiency D&C costs $650/ft down 8% YoY, digital AI boosting EURs 12-15%, EOR adding 5 Mbbl/d. Risks: weather, inflation hedged 80%, regulatory with electric fracs cutting emissions 25%.

I will now turn the call over to David Rodriguez for an operational update.

David Rodriguez: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 525,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Maverick Pad online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, including electrification and AI optimizations that have lowered LOE and boosted efficiencies across basins.

Now I will turn it over to Lisa Chen for an update on our exploration activities.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. Good morning, everyone. Today, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our exploration and drilling activities for Q3 2024, focusing on key well results and forward plans. We've executed our capital-efficient D&C program with WTI at $82/bbl and Henry Hub at $3.10/MMBtu, focused on high-return Permian inventory plus offshore and international plays.

In Q3, we spudded 28 wells and brought online 32 gross operated wells, 95% success rate, 15% sequential completion increase. Drilling costs $6.8 million/well, down 8% QoQ and 12% YoY with PDC bits and 11,500-ft laterals. Permian 85%: Delaware Maverick Pad six Wolfcamp A/B laterals, State Blackcomb 145H-1 at 1,850 boe/d IP30 (78% oil), 22% above type curve, 1.4 Mboe EUR via geosteering and LWD. Bighorn 3-mile at 1,650 boe/d, 15% uplift from 55-stage fracs. Midland Pecos pad 1,120 boe/d IP30, 105-day cycles.

Offshore GoM Winterfell 25% WI WF-2 sidetrack 8,500 boe/d gross IP (95% liquids), net 140,000 boe Q3, de-risking 50 MMboe via FWI. Namibia Orange-1X 85 ft oil pay, 20% porosity, potential 10,000 boe/d IP. Efficiencies: Permian 850 ft/day, 25% less flat time, 120 bpm pumping.

Future: 120-130 wells 2024, 70% Permian, $850-900M D&C capex, third rig Q1, extended reach tests. 60% FCF to returns above $75 WTI, 12,000 acres bolt-on, all-electric fracs cutting emissions 30%, 1.2 MMBoe DvD at sub-$50/boe.

We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 25 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Robert Hayes to discuss our marketing strategy.

Robert Hayes: Thank you, Lisa. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. Good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to dive into our Midstream segment performance for Q3 2024, focusing on transportation volumes and infrastructure development. Midstream is a cornerstone of our integrated model, delivering high-margin, fee-based revenues insulating from volatility. We transported a record 2.8 MMboe/d, up 12% YoY and 4% QoQ, driving $425 million segment EBITDA, 18% YoY up, 62% margins from 92% utilization.

Crude 1.6 MMbbl/d (57%), up 15% YoY; Permian Whittenburg Pipeline 820,000 bbl/d (96% util), Permian rigs ~300, flaring <1%. WTI-Brent discount $3/bbl from $8. Gas 10.2 Bcf/d up 9%, Gulf Coast Express 2.1 Bcf/d to Agua Dulce amid 14.5 Bcf/d exports. NGL 1.05 MMbbl/d up 11%, Mont Belvieu $0.75/gal. Appalachia 3.8 Bcf/d (85% contracted Mountain Valley), Bakken 450,000 bbl/d.

Revenues $720 million up 14%, 95% fee-based 10-year terms, $25M deficiency. Minor Gulf NGL dip normalized. CapEx $1.2B 2024, 65% YTD: Permian Highway Phase II +300,000 bbl/d online Oct, $450M JV under budget, 98% contracted $120M EBITDA. Apex LNG Connector 1.2 Bcf/d FID Q1 2025.

Sustainability: 150 miles DAS leak detection saving 15% integrity CapEx, drone ILI 40% crude cutting downtime 22%, CCUS 2 MMtpa 2025 with Occidental. 70% EBITDA inflation-indexed to 2035, 12-15% IRRs. Q4 2.9 MMboe/d, FY EBITDA $1.65-1.70B.

We are seeing strong demand for expanded pipeline capacity in the Permian Basin, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen relationships. The impact of these infrastructure projects is significant.

I will now turn it over to Emily Carter to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Robert. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We've made significant progress on cutting greenhouse gas emissions, with Permian electrification at 40% of pads reducing diesel 25% and Scope 1 intensity 15-30%, all-electric fracs aligning with net-zero 2040. Investments in renewables, water management via SWD to 150,000 BWPD, biodiversity protection, DAS for leaks, CCUS hubs 2 MMtpa, methane rules compliance with electric fracs 20% activity, green bonds tied to KPIs, and CO2 EOR pilots boosting recovery. Drone ILI, AI maintenance, and LNG tech with DRU for 20% lower methane.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Joe Harris with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Joe Harris: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production guidance for next quarter and full year?

Mike Thompson: Good morning, Joe. As Sarah detailed, Q4 guidance is 530-540k BOE/d with oil growth from Permian TILs offsetting declines, full year 1.16-1.24 MMBOE/d. Key drivers include operational momentum in Permian with PowerFracs, regional tailwinds from OPEC+, efficiencies like AI reservoir sims adding 12-15% EURs, EOR scaling to 5 Mbbl/d. Risks like weather and inflation are mitigant with hedges and flex capex to 20% cut, prioritizing FCF at 45-55% EBITDAX yield.

Operator: Our next question comes from Anna Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Anna Lee: Good morning. What are your expectations for commodity prices and their impact?

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning, Anna. With WTI $75-85 strip, Brent $78-88, Henry Hub $2.50-3.50, we're hedged 65% 2024 oil at $78, 60% gas at $3.20 floor. OPEC+ cuts support oil, LNG oversupply caps gas but Permian/LNG ramps provide upside. This supports our cash margins above $45/boe breakeven, enabling returns and growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera: Could you please provide more color on operational cost reductions?

David Rodriguez: Good morning, Tom. We've driven drilling costs down 12% YoY to $6.8M/well, D&C $650/ft, LOE $8.50/boe via electrification, AI cutting downtime 20%, cycle times 95-105 days, frac efficiencies 120 bpm. Permian 850 ft/day, refracs at $2M/well 40% uplift, SWD expansions cutting disposal 20%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Lisa Chen: Thanks, Rachel. Exceptional results like Maverick outperformance 22%, Winterfell de-risking 50 MMboe, Namibia potential blockbuster shift strategy toward longer laterals 15k ft, third rig activation, bolt-ons high-grading to 7 years inventory. Prioritizes Tier 1 at sub-$50 returns, 60% FCF returns, ESG-aligned growth with 1.2 MMBoe DvD.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Patel with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Brian Patel: What is the outlook for the new midstream infrastructure in the coming years?

Robert Hayes: Good morning, Brian. Permian Highway Phase II already 98% contracted at 15% IRR, LNG Connector FID Q1 2025 for LNG wave to 25 Bcf/d by 2028, adds 500k boe/d capacity YE25. Q4 volumes 2.9 MMboe/d, FY EBITDA $1.65-1.70B, 16% growth, de-risked with MWAs to 2035, capturing Permian 6.5 MMbbl/d.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sophia Grant with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sophia Grant: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Emily Carter: Good morning, Sophia. Targets include net-zero 2040, Scope 1 cuts 25% YoY via electric fracs 20-40%, methane <1%, CCUS 2 MMtpa 2025, DAS 150 miles saving 15% CapEx, drone ILI 22% less downtime, EOR recovery uplift, green bonds KPIs, IRA incentives positioning for premium financing.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
